newsitem.title: USA: Apple confident can sustain profit by FY Q2.
newsitem.headline: Apple confident can sustain profit by FY Q2.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Gilbert Amelio said the company is confident it can achieve sustained profitability by the end of its fiscal 1997 second quarter.
"We remain confident about reaching sustainable profitability by the end of Q2 '97," Amelio said in a statement released with Apple's fiscal fourth quarter results.
Apple Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson said the company had positive cash flow from operations of $410 million in the quarter.
"We continue to make progress in strengthening Apple's financial condition, as our $410 million in positive cash flow from operations during the quarter suggests," said Anderson.
Amelio said the company has already achieved some of the objectives he introduced since taking over at the head of the troubled computer maker in February.
"By increasing revenues sequentially and fortifying Apple's financial position in each of the last two quarters, we have achieved two very critical goals of Apple's transition," Amelio said.
"As we move forward, our challenges will be to extend our competitive leadership in key markets and to reclaim the mantle of industry pioneer and innovator," he added.
Apple said it espects the mix of its products to shift towards more consumer-oriented products, with PowerBooks in ramp-up mode through the next two quarters.

"Beginning in the second (March) quarter, Apple expects to begin to experience some modest year-over-year growth," the company said. "Apple feels good about its ability to sustain gross margins at or above the 20 percent level, and expect to hold operating expenses to around $500 million a quarter.
